instruction: Browse LEGO sets for kids and sort by highest price.

metadata.explanation: Task requires browsing LEGO products in Kids/Toys category and sorting by price high-low (S=5). Similar 3-step navigation pattern as original. Evaluator checks URL parameters and HTML elements for correct filtering and sorting. No custom functions needed - uses existing active_tab_html_parse getter and check_direct_json_object metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: LEGO category, Kids/Toys filtering, and sorting by highest price
Dual verification approach (HTML class elements + URL parameters) provides robust checking with good redundancy
The getter logic properly extracts breadcrumb navigation elements (pmpSearch_breadcrumb) to verify category path
URL parameter checking (S=5 for Price High-Low, LEGO/Toys/Kids keywords) correctly validates the sorting and filtering state
Expected values are semantically correct: all required filters should be true, no unexpected elements should exist
Case-insensitive matching handles variations in website display (LEGO vs lego)
The metric correctly compares boolean values for each requirement
Complete coverage: checks LEGO (2 ways), Toys (2 ways), Kids (2 ways), Price High-Low (2 ways), and unexpected elements
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor concern: HTML class names (pmpSearch_breadcrumb, sbSelector) are site-specific and could break if Kohls.com redesigns their website structure
Consider adding postconfig to ensure the page has fully loaded before verification, as dynamic content might load asynchronously
The evaluator assumes specific class names exist on Kohls.com - if the website structure changes, this will fail (but this is acceptable for the current task)
